extracted.intended_audience: editors of surgical journals, surgical researchers, and authors preparing randomized controlled trials or systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and reporting which elements surgical journals instruct authors to include (e.g., COI, URM, trial registration, CONSORT, PRISMA) and how widely these reporting guidelines are endorsed. Useful for editors updating instructions and authors preparing manuscripts for surgical journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interests (COI) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Author guidelines should require disclosure of conflicts of interest (COI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the surveyed surgical journals, guidance on COI was present in 82% of journals. Journals with editorial offices in the UK were more likely to insist on disclosure of COI. Editors are advised to include uniform COI disclosure requirements in instructions to authors to improve publication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Requirements for Manuscripts (URM) adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should reference or require adherence to the Uniform Requirements for Manuscripts (URM) published for biomedical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URM endorsement was found in 62% of the sampled surgical journals. Including URM in author instructions provides standardised expectations for manuscript preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Author instructions should require registration of clinical trials (prospective trial registration) as a condition for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 32% of surveyed surgical journals endorsed trial registration. Higher-impact journals were more likely to adopt trial registration. Editors should consider mandating trial registration to improve transparency and reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT endorsement for randomized controlled trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should formally endorse and require reporting of randomized controlled trials according to the CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT endorsement appeared in 29% of surgical journals surveyed. Higher-impact journals were more likely to adopt CONSORT, and UK-based editorial offices more likely to endorse it. The authors recommend uniform endorsement of CONSORT in instructions to authors to improve trial reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA endorsement for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should formally endorse and require reporting of systematic reviews and meta-analyses according to the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA was endorsed by only 10% of surveyed surgical journals. Adoption was more likely among higher-impact journals. The paper concludes that limited endorsement of PRISMA may contribute to poorer quality of published systematic reviews and recommends that editors update author instructions to endorse PRISMA.
